Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Kitchen, meals & drinks

ice cream noun

modern

Helfer, Lexicon auxiliare
Vox Latina (via Morgan–Owens)

1A modern word, a back-formation from Italian gelato; classically gelātus is only the participle “frozen, set”. Recorded by Helfer’s Lexicon auxiliare and Vox Latina (via Morgan–Owens’s online index). Ruling: gelātum for ice cream.

gelātum1, gelātī n.

noun, second declension

The nearest Roman thing: Pliny’s dessert of halica cum mulsō et nive (Ep. 1.15.2).

Other words

  • 2cremum: short e (Traupman crēmum, pp. 298, 331, 406). Lewis & Short crĕmum, from its one ancient instance (Ven. Fort. 11.14.1); Traupman himself prints cremum on pp. 67 and 71.

    congelidum cremum2

    also used · modern · Traupman 71

    Also gelidum cremum, in his glossary (p. 331).

  • glaciēs dulcis / edūlis

    also used · modern · M-O s.v. ice cream

  • nix dulcis

    also used · modern · M-O s.v. ice cream

  • sorbillum glaciātum

    also used · modern · Lexicon Recentis Latinitatis, via Morgan–Owens

Examples

  • Vīs gelātum?

    Do you want ice cream?composed

See also flavour, kind, dessert.
